verdict.rationale: Zep's open-source Graphiti framework lets you build and query a Context Graph locally, and the pricing page lists a "Your VPC" deployment option. But the evidence never shows the full Zep memory service (users, threads, Context Blocks) being self-hosted from open-source code, and gives no Docker or deployment instructions. The VPC option appears to be a commercial tier rather than open-source self-hosting. missing for 10: Docker or container deployment docs, evidence that the full Zep memory service (not just the Graphiti framework) is open-source and self-hostable, self-host setup or infra guidance, independent hands-on corroboration of self-hosting.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the memory layer from open-source code (e.g. via Docker) on infrastructure I control

citations.quote: Graphiti is the open-source temporal knowledge graph framework. Use it to build and query a single Context Graph per subject locally
Thank you for open sourcing this!
